newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian stocks slip in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian stocks slip in listless trade.

text.p: Norwegian share prices were a notch lower on Tuesday with few impulses to offer direction in thin dealings, brokers said.
The market came under pressure as oil-sensitive stocks Norsk Hydro and Saga Petroleum slipped back on declines in the oil price.
The Total share index closed 0.4 percent down at 839.71 points. Turnover was a meagre 451 million crowns.
"It was really slow today, the momentum wasn't there," said one dealer. "Everyone was waiting for the U.S. (industrial production) figures but they had little impact."
Industrial giant Norsk Hydro, which has a weighting of around 20 percent in the Total index, relinquished 4.50 crowns to close at 301 crowns.
Saga Petroleum gave up 1.50 crowns in the A share and 0.50 crowns in the B's to end at 104 and 94 crowns respectively.

Dealers said slight profit taking put downward pressure on engineering and offshore group Aker, which dipped 1.50 crowns to 133 crowns. Aker stock has climbed to near year highs recently on speculation of a merger with investment group RGI, the company's largest shareholder.
